To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a physically based 2D-infiltration and runoff model is developed and evaluated with the literature data and it is found that the model performed equally well.
the developed infiltration model is simple, easy to understand, and can be used for infiltration prediction in uniform and layered soil columns.
the infiltration rate decreases with the formation of the surface seal and the infiltration rate decreases when the seal is saturated.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a simple physically based 1-D infiltration model for irrigated soil.
the development of an infiltration model for seal formed or seal-free uniform or layered soil column.
the development of a physically based infiltration model that includes the effect of seal and its thickness on infiltration.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the developed model is simple to use and can be used for irrigation planning and design.
the developed infiltration model is simple, robust and can be used for predicting infiltration through seal free and seal formed uniform and three-layered soils.
the developed infiltration model can be used for infiltration prediction through uniform or layered soil columns with and without surface seals.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the developed model can be used for irrigation scheduling in irrigated agriculture.
the developed 1D infiltration model can predict the infiltration process through seal free uniform soil up to 360 min, seal formed uniform up to 240 min and seal formed layered up to 120 min.
the infiltration model, which is developed in this study, can be used in irrigation scheduling, water management, water conservation and water quality management studies.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the developed model can be used as a simple approach for predicting infiltration in irrigated soils and can be incorporated in crop models to improve the prediction of crop water requirements and crop yields.
the developed model can be used to estimate infiltration in uniform and layered soil profiles with seal and without seal.
surface seal affects infiltration through irrigated soils, and hence, inclusion in the infiltration models is essential.
